senses.gloss:
1. पथ् पथ्, i. 1, Par. To go.
 --† i. 10, पाथय, To throw (v. r.).

पथ पथ,
 1. m. Way, reach, Rām. 3, 56, 3.
 2. Latter part of comp. words = पथिन्, A way, a road. अ-, m. A wrong way. अपत्य-, m. The vulva. अर्ध-, m. The half of a way. आर्य-, m. The road of the honourable ones. उत्तरा- and उदक्पथ, i. e. उदञ्च्-, m. The northern country. कुसिद-, m. An usurious way, Man. 8, 152. जल-, m. A sea voyage. त्रि-, n. Heaven, earth, and the infernal regions. दक्षिणा-, m. The southern country. दर्शन-, m. Sight. दिक्पथ, i. e. दिश्-, m. The road of the country, Rājat. 5, 341. [] दृक्पथ, i. e. दृश्-, m. Sight, Vikr. d. 95. धर्म-, m. The road of virtue. धूम-, m. A sacrifice, Bhāg. P. 4, 4, 10. नक्षत्र-, m. The starred heaven. नयन-, m. Sight, Vedāntas. in Chr. 206, 1. पाषण्ड-, m. The way of the heretics, Daśak. in Chr. 185, 6. बणिक्पथ, i. e. बणिज्-, m. Trade, Man. 1, 90. रोमराजि-, i. e. रोमन्-राजि- (m.), A line of hair extending to the navel; in तनुरोम-राजिपथ, The waist, Śiś. 9, 22. वि-, m. A bad road. श्री-, m. A highway. सत्प्˚, i. e. सन्त्- (ptcple. pres. of 1. अस्), m.
 1. A good road.
 2. Correct conduct. सु-,
 I. adj. Having good roads, Lass. 97, 2 (था, ved. for थानि).
 II. m.
 1. A good road.
 2. Good conduct.
 --Cf. πάτος; A.S. padh.
पथिक पथिक, i. e. पथ + इक, m. A traveller, Pañc. 245, 4.

पथिन् पथिन्, for पन्थन् (cf. परिपन्थिन्), which is the base of some cases, the bases of some others is पथ्, the nom. and voc. sing. पन्थास्, m.
 1. A road, a way, Megh. 28.
 2. The name of a hell, Man. 4, 90.
 --Comp.
 --Cf. Lat. pons, pontis, and perhaps ponto, pontonis.

पथ्य पथ्य, i. e. पथ + य,
 I. adj., f. या, Furthering, Böhtl. Ind. Spr. 448. Fit, suitable, salutary, Pañc. 69, 17.
 II. f. या, Yellow myrobalan, Terminalia chebula.
 --Comp.
पाथस् पा + थस्, n. Water, Kathās. 27, 122.

पाथेय पाथेय, i. e. पथिन् + एय, n. Provisions for a journey, Vikr. d. 94.
 --Comp.
पाथोज पाथोज, i. e. पाथस्-ज, n. A lotus, Rājat. 4, 110.
पाथोधर पाथोधर, i. e. पाथस्-धर, m. A cloud, Rājat. 3, 202.
पाथोधि पाथोधि, i. e. पाथस्-धा (see पयोधि), m. The ocean, Rājat. 3, 68.
